walkthroughs.body_html:
Coordination & Control — a core area of GCSE Biology.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Coordination & Control brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Coordination & Control.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Adrenaline binds to receptors on the membrane and activates:
options: DNA directly
Adenylyl cyclase to make cAMP
Ribosomes
Lysosomes

mcqs.q: Which gland is referred to as the master gland?
options: Pancreas
Pituitary
Thyroid
Adrenal

mcqs.q: What is the role of the guide RNA in CRISPR-Cas9?
options: Guide RNA is the new sequence that gets inserted into the genome.
Guide RNA is the enzyme that cuts the DNA.
It directs Cas9 to the specific DNA sequence to cut by base-pairing with the target.
Plants only respire at night and only photosynthesise during the day; the processes never overlap.
Plants only respire at night and only photosynthesise during the day; the processes never overlap.
Missense and silent mutations always produce a non-functional protein.
Plants only photosynthesise and do not respire; respiration is for animals only.
Yes — plants respire all the time to release energy; they also photosynthesise when there is light.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between a silent and a missense mutation?
options: A silent mutation changes a base but the codon still codes for the same amino acid; a missense mutation changes the amino acid encoded.
Missense and silent mutations always produce a non-functional protein.
A silent mutation has no effect because no base actually changes.
Plants only respire at night and only photosynthesise during the day; the processes never overlap.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Adrenaline”?
options: Peptide hormone from β cells of pancreas; lowers blood glucose by stimulating uptake and glycogenesis.
Peptide hormone from α cells of pancreas; raises blood glucose by promoting glycogenolysis and gluconeogenesis.
Chemical messenger secreted into the bloodstream and acting on target cells with complementary receptors.
Steroid? No: catecholamine secreted by adrenal medulla; activates fight-or-flight, raising heart rate and blood glucose.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Insulin”?
options: Chemical messenger secreted into the bloodstream and acting on target cells with complementary receptors.
Steroid? No: catecholamine secreted by adrenal medulla; activates fight-or-flight, raising heart rate and blood glucose.
Peptide hormone from β cells of pancreas; lowers blood glucose by stimulating uptake and glycogenesis.
Ductless gland secreting hormones directly into the blood, e.g. pituitary, thyroid, pancreas.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Glucagon”?
options: Chemical messenger secreted into the bloodstream and acting on target cells with complementary receptors.
Peptide hormone from α cells of pancreas; raises blood glucose by promoting glycogenolysis and gluconeogenesis.
Steroid? No: catecholamine secreted by adrenal medulla; activates fight-or-flight, raising heart rate and blood glucose.
Ductless gland secreting hormones directly into the blood, e.g. pituitary, thyroid, pancreas.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Hormone”?
options: Ductless gland secreting hormones directly into the blood, e.g. pituitary, thyroid, pancreas.
Chemical messenger secreted into the bloodstream and acting on target cells with complementary receptors.
Peptide hormone from β cells of pancreas; lowers blood glucose by stimulating uptake and glycogenesis.
Intracellular molecule (e.g. cAMP) that relays a signal from a hormone-receptor binding to enzymes inside the cell.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Second messenger”?
options: Peptide hormone from β cells of pancreas; lowers blood glucose by stimulating uptake and glycogenesis.
Intracellular molecule (e.g. cAMP) that relays a signal from a hormone-receptor binding to enzymes inside the cell.
Peptide hormone from α cells of pancreas; raises blood glucose by promoting glycogenolysis and gluconeogenesis.
Steroid? No: catecholamine secreted by adrenal medulla; activates fight-or-flight, raising heart rate and blood glucose.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Endocrine gland”?
options: Chemical messenger secreted into the bloodstream and acting on target cells with complementary receptors.
Ductless gland secreting hormones directly into the blood, e.g. pituitary, thyroid, pancreas.
Steroid? No: catecholamine secreted by adrenal medulla; activates fight-or-flight, raising heart rate and blood glucose.
Peptide hormone from β cells of pancreas; lowers blood glucose by stimulating uptake and glycogenesis.
